item.title: Stormwater directorate objects to Transport Malta's Bormla car park plan
item.description: The Coastal and Stormwater Directorate formally objected to Transport Malta's proposal to replace the historic reservoir outside St Helen's Gate in Bormla with a new reservoir and car park, warning the project would compromise an existing rainwater-harvesting facility and destroy significant remains of a mid-19th century industrial reservoir.
item.content:encoded:

Sources: Malta Today

item.title: Former soldier Lorin Scicluna jailed eight years for racially motivated hit-and-run
item.description: Judge Natasha Galea Sciberras sentenced Scicluna to eight years in prison after a jury found him guilty by six votes to three of grievously injuring May Malimi in a hit-and-run on 1 February 2019, and of driving without registration plates. He was also ordered to pay €6,676.32 in court expert fees. The judge said he could have faced up to 12 years but that the Attorney General's bill of indictment requested a maximum of nine, and stressed the court wanted to send a clear warning against racial hatred, noting he committed the offence while serving in the Armed Forces. The sentence follows his acquittal last Sunday of the murder of Lassana Cisse and the attempted murders of three others. A coalition of 23 civil society organisations welcomed the sentence but called it "partial justice" and accused the prosecution of failing to deliver justice.

Sources: Times of Malta, Malta Independent, Malta Today, Lovin Malta, Newsbook

item.title: Standards commissioner finds PN's Joe Giglio breached ethics rules over tax evasion bill
item.description: Standards Commissioner Joseph Azzopardi concluded that Giglio was obliged to declare an interest before parliament approved the August 2025 bill allowing tax dodgers to settle instead of facing court, because he was then legal representative of Nigel and Mikaela Scerri, owners of Ennesse, who faced a €1.5 million tax evasion and money laundering case later dropped under the new law. The commissioner ruled the failure was a minor breach, and Giglio, who voted against the bill, rejected the finding and refused to apologise, calling the interpretation of conflict-of-interest rules "almost absurd".

item.title: A fifth of Gozo tourism establishments had a worse summer than 2025
item.description: A Gozo Tourism Association survey covering June to September found 43.08% of establishments performed at the same level as 2025, 35.38% improved and 21.54% declined. Power cuts were the leading challenge, cited by 64.6% of respondents, ahead of operating costs and traffic, and 47.69% rated summer revenue as average, 40% good and 12.31% poor.

item.title: Fifteen Maltese passengers stranded after US coast guard detains cruise ship in Miami
item.description: At least 15 Maltese holidaymakers boarded the MSC Poesia in Miami for a 12-day Caribbean cruise but never sailed after the US Coast Guard detained the vessel at the port. The ship remained stuck for four days before MSC Cruises cancelled the voyage and told passengers to leave by Thursday noon. Reports said the Coast Guard identified deficiencies with systems on board, though passengers were told the hold-up was not for safety reasons.

item.title: National Archives launches 2035 strategy with new centre and digitisation push
item.description: The Ministry for the Arts, Culture and National Heritage launched the National Archives' Strategic Vision 2035 alongside a new institutional identity, "It-Tila Minsuħa" (The Woven Canvas). Plans include a new national archives centre, improved infrastructure in Gozo, greater digitisation of holdings and expanded public access to Malta's documentary record.

item.title: Agius Saliba secures EU backing for probe into Temu's €3 charge on Maltese shoppers
item.description: Labour MEP Alex Agius Saliba obtained unanimous support from coordinators of the European Parliament's Petitions Committee for a discussion in January on his petition concerning the €3 charge applied by Temu and other online platforms. The petition asks for an investigation into whether Maltese consumers pay more than shoppers in larger EU member states because of Malta's geography, and calls on the European Commission to give clear answers.

item.title: Momentum protests exclusion from televised Budget 2027 debates
item.description: Momentum said it had formally written to Public Broadcasting Services and the Broadcasting Authority to protest its exclusion from televised discussions on the 2027 Budget, arguing that public broadcasting should reflect a wider range of political opinion. The party cited TVM programming and said state and mainstream media marginalise alternative political voices, protecting the traditional two-party system.

item.title: Planning Authority approves Siġġiewi zoo expansion with nearly €57,000 in fines
item.description: The Planning Authority sanctioned unauthorised development at L-Arka ta' Noè Zoo in Siġġiewi, allowing new enclosures, stables and parking on land outside the development zone. The applicant, Anton Caruana Cutajar, must pay a €31,869.92 fine for sanctioning irregularities plus a €25,000 contribution to the Planning Authority's Planning Fund. The site covers 32,000 square metres, of which about 18,100 are already occupied by zoo facilities.

item.title: Gżira residents say they were blocked from Facebook group over Manoel Island padel courts
item.description: Maltese actor Thomas Camilleri says administrators of the "Gżira Residents" Facebook group deleted posts and blocked members who opposed the disputed padel courts on Manoel Island, and that residents protesting hotels in Triq ir-Rebħa were also removed. He claims administrators are linked to Gżira Football Club and to the club president's interests. Sharlon Pace, whose brother is behind one of the proposed hotels, called the allegations "all lies". The group has since been made private and a rival group set up.

item.description: The airline said the new route between Malta and Bordeaux, France, will operate twice a week, every Monday and Thursday, as part of its expanded European network for the summer season, giving passengers a direct link to the Nouvelle-Aquitaine region of south-western France.

item.title: Twenty-one social housing properties vacant in Gozo, parliamentary answer reveals
item.description: Housing Minister Owen Bonnici told MP Frank Anthony Tabone that the Housing Authority holds 338 residential properties in Gozo for social accommodation, of which 21 are currently vacant but only 19 are available for allocation. The remaining two are being reserved, and the authority is seeking to allocate the vacant units to persons and families in need of housing.

item.title: Hotels and restaurants association backs on-the-spot cannabis fines for tourists
item.description: The Malta Hotels and Restaurants Association welcomed plans announced by Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield to impose on-the-spot fines for cannabis-related offences involving tourists, saying visible police enforcement and immediate action are needed to deter offences and keep Malta a safe and attractive destination. Bedingfield said public cannabis smoking will carry a €235 penalty under the on-the-spot fines system.

item.title: Pet sitting operator fined €3,000 after two dogs die in Żejtun attack

The court found he had failed to adequately safeguard the animals entrusted to him and fined him €3,000.

item.title: Court freezes €57.8 million in assets of man accused of running Malta money laundering network
item.description: A court froze assets worth €57,812,396.08 and a further $132,900 belonging to Nasr Edin Jeray, a 53-year-old Libyan national residing in Żurrieq, after he was charged with money laundering, carrying out unlicensed banking and financial services, criminal association and participation in a criminal organisation. Police arrested him on Wednesday following a financial investigation into a wider network suspected of running for several years, and the court also ordered the seizure of four vehicles including three BMWs and a Toyota Yaris, together with a Lithuanian Revolut account. The prosecutor opposed release but the court granted bail with strict conditions, including a €20,000 deposit, a €100,000 personal guarantee, no travel, no contact with witnesses and signing the bail book twice daily.

item.title: Pet sitter acquitted over deaths of two Pomeranians mauled by Huskies
item.description: Terry Caruana, 50, was acquitted of animal cruelty charges over the deaths of two Pomeranians attacked by three Huskies at his 'Pets R Us' boarding facility in Triq Alfredo Cachia, Żejtun, in December 2022, after the court found insufficient evidence of criminal negligence, but was fined €3,000 for operating the establishment without a licence. The dogs had escaped after chewing through a plastic lock on their enclosure while the accused was temporarily away. Magistrate Kevan Azzopardi acknowledged the tragic circumstances but found the prosecution had not proved its case.

item.title: Planning Board revives Mġarr petrol station relocation permit
item.description: The Planning Authority restored the validity of a 2012 permission to move the Mġarr Square petrol station to agricultural land in Żebbiegħ, reversing its earlier decision to declare it null and void over unmet public-deed obligations. The applicant, Michael Galea, has undertaken to close and decommission the existing station and garage and clear illegal storage yards, with a 36-month works programme and an additional €50,000 bank guarantee. A separate renewal application remains pending and must be assessed on its own merits, and Din l-Art Ħelwa has already objected.

item.title: Elderly passenger grievously injured in Għasri crash into wall and power pole
item.description: Two elderly women were injured at around 11am on Thursday when a Mazda Demio driven by a 72-year-old woman from Żebbuġ collided with a wall and an electricity pole on Triq iż-Żebbuġ in Għasri, Gozo. The 71-year-old passenger was certified as having sustained grievous injuries, while the driver suffered slight injuries. Civil Protection Department members attended the scene and both women were taken to Gozo General Hospital by ambulance. Police investigations are ongoing.

item.title: CRPD lifts blanket ban on ABA therapy refunds after Ombudsman intervention
item.description: The Commission for the Rights of Persons with Disability has withdrawn its blanket refusal to refund Applied Behaviour Analysis therapy for children, following an Education Commissioner intervention after a mother's complaint to the Ombudsman. The commissioner called the policy "unreasonable, unjust, improperly discriminatory and wrong in principle" given that ABA-based services are funded by the state in other settings. Applications submitted since the scheme was introduced in 2023 are now being reviewed, and the CRPD has undertaken to publish a list of qualifying ABA therapists.

item.title: More than 35,500 students enrolled in post-secondary and tertiary education
item.description: National data for the 2024-25 academic year show post-secondary enrolments rising 4.7 per cent to 10,886 students and tertiary enrolments up 10.6 per cent to 24,647, an overall increase of 8.7 per cent. Men still outnumber women at post-secondary level by 2.7 percentage points, while women made up 54.1 per cent of tertiary students. Foreign students accounted for 18.6 per cent of post-secondary enrolment, and 84.5 per cent of post-secondary students attend state institutions.

item.title: GWU and AFTA seek memorandum to soften Budget 2027 impact on foreign workers
item.description: The General Workers' Union and the Association of Foreign Temping Agencies met at the Workers' Memorial Building to discuss practical measures that could ease the effect of Budget 2027 provisions on third-country nationals working in Malta, with a Memorandum of Understanding under discussion. GWU secretary general Kevin Camilleri said the union considers the budget forward-looking but has reservations about measures affecting third-country nationals, while AFTA president Fabio Muscat said the collaboration is important for those affected. AFTA presented several proposals for discussion.

item.title: 80 academics demand independent review of Malta's jury system after murder acquittals
item.description: Eighty academics wrote to Prime Minister Robert Abela expressing "profound dismay and concern" over the acquittals in the cases concerning the murders of Daphne Caruana Galizia and Lassana Cisse, saying they raised serious questions about public confidence and the effectiveness of the jury system. Without questioning judicial independence or the presumption of innocence, the signatories asked for an independent technical committee to review the system's effectiveness, safeguards, procedures and transparency, and to propose concrete legal, procedural or institutional reforms.

item.title: Sliema church objects to 24-room boutique hotel planned metres away
item.description: Sacro Cuor Parish Church has objected to planning application PA/06783/26 for a 24-room boutique hotel with rooftop pool on Triq San Trofimu, metres from the Grade 1 listed church, warning that hotel guests could complain about the bells and demand restrictions on their ringing. The parish said the project is "excessive for this sensitive location" and would harm the historic character of a street only four metres wide that is regularly closed for funerals and processions. NGO Flimkien għal Ambjent Aħjar is also urging residents to object, citing loss of garden space and traffic concerns.

item.title: Man granted bail after smashing daughter's salon window, injuring her and ex-wife
item.description: A 44-year-old financial controller from Birkirkara was granted bail after pleading guilty to smashing the glass front of his daughter's hair salon in Birkirkara on 1 October, sending shards into her face and that of his former wife. The daughter was grievously injured and the former wife slightly injured, and the accused made threats towards police officers while being treated in hospital. Bail was granted against a €300 deposit, a €10,000 personal guarantee and a protection order, with sentencing to follow and a suspended sentence and treatment order agreed.

item.title: Eurostat: 55.9% of Maltese young people encounter hostile messages online
item.description: Eurostat figures show 55.9% of internet users aged 16 to 29 in Malta encountered hostile or degrading messages online in 2025, slightly above the EU average of 54.2% and the tenth-highest rate among the 22 EU countries covered. Ireland led the chart at 78%, followed by Finland at 76.6% and France at 64.6%, while Greece recorded the lowest rate at 33.2%. The data measures exposure to such content among recent internet users and does not necessarily indicate personal targeting.

item.title: Archbishop Scicluna and President visit Maltese patients receiving care in London
item.description: Archbishop Charles Scicluna revealed for the first time that an accident in Turkey in May, when he tripped over the dais during a visit to the Ecumenical Patriarch in Istanbul, tore a tendon in his knee and left him facing "lifelong disability" without surgery. He spoke during his annual pastoral visit to Maltese patients in London, alongside President Myriam Spiteri Debono, who visited Great Ormond Street Hospital to meet a three-year-old Maltese girl undergoing specialised treatment. Officials said 40 Maltese patients are currently in the UK for ongoing consultations and follow-up tests, with support from the Malta Community Chest Fund and religious orders.

Home Affairs and Security Minister Glenn Bedingfield confirmed in reply to a parliamentary question that works have been completed in some prison divisions, where the system started operating in September, with installation continuing in other parts and expected to finish in the coming weeks.

item.title: PN says Budget 2027 ignores long-standing health and Gozo pledges
item.description: Shadow ministers for health and Gozo, Stephen Spiteri and Frank Anthony Tabone, said the government presented another budget that "does not seriously address" health and Gozo problems. They listed waiting lists at St Luke's and Karin Grech Hospital, cancer medicines not fully on the formulary, healthcare worker burnout, underinvestment in mental health and long-running Gozo infrastructure such as the Gozo hospital, Mġarr port, Gozo court, power cuts and the Marsalforn breakwater as unresolved. The PN also criticised the scaling back of the private insurance service that had eased pressure on Mater Dei emergency services.

item.title: Borg tells Commonwealth leaders small economies must not be left behind in investment
item.description: Deputy Prime Minister and Health Minister Ian Borg led the Maltese delegation to the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting 2026 in Antigua and Barbuda, where he argued that investment must reach smaller economies, which need well-prepared projects with clear implementation plans to attract financing. He said Malta's experience with an open economy, connectivity, stability and investment in skills shows how small states can prosper, and that investment should be measured by the jobs, stronger local businesses, new skills and technology use it leaves behind. He also met King Charles III.
